current.text: He is projected as Denver's 10th man, coming off the bench. The projected starters are Murray, Braun, Cam Johnson, Gordon and Jokic.
He finished 427th in fantasy value last season.
His age-24 season is the time for him to show something.
Moore expects him to start the season at about 15 minutes a night. The team's goal is to get him to 20.
He will not start at shooting guard or small forward on a healthy roster. He could start only if Braun is traded or Murray is out.
Denver's roster is unsettled. Braun and Cam Johnson are possible trade pieces, and Moore expects at least two of last year's starters to be gone by the deadline.
Losing Tim Hardaway Jr. leaves Denver short on spacing, and the team needs shooters who will fire away off Jokic's gravity.
Moore sees him as a positive bench player but does not predict a breakout because his opportunity is uncertain.

durable.text: Experts disagree on his shooting. One calls him an elite shooter. Another calls his shooting spotty.
He adds little beyond shooting: few rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, and few free throw attempts.
His three-point attempt rate has dropped each season while his two-point rate has risen.
He is becoming more than a three-point shooter. He has a phenomenal floater game and can hit corner threes and spot-up shots.
His defense needs a big jump.

tags.name: minutes competition
tags.detail: 10th man behind Murray and Braun on the wings, with about 15 minutes expected and opportunity uncertain

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 334, ESPN rank 302) and he was not drafted last season, so he is not a pick in our 144-player auction. His projected line of about 7.7 points and 1.2 threes, with almost nothing in REB, AST, STL or BLK, has no category outlier to build around. Low turnovers are his only plus. He matters only if his minutes move toward 20 or he becomes a starter. Watch for a Braun trade or a Murray injury early in the season.
